name: Soul Glo
label: Epitaph
lede: Soul Glo started in Philadelphia for kids who fit neither the city's punk shows nor its hardcore ones. Now the band has a Pitchfork 8.5, a Coachella set and a bass slot that keeps changing hands.

eras.title: Outsiders in every room
eras.text: Pierce Jordan and Ruben Polo start a band in Philadelphia for kids who fit neither the city's hardcore shows nor its punk ones. Two untitled records and a Missouri highway arrest later, the lineup that makes the big records is in place.

years.cap: Soul Glo at a basement show, April 2015
years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Loud Fast Philly · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: Pierce Jordan and Ruben Polo start Soul Glo in Philadelphia
years.p: [[Pierce Jordan|6a8a8824-41e0-422e-a17e-b9b0517d89f2]] sings, Ruben Polo plays guitar, Ethan Brennan plays bass and Jamie Sokol drums.
years.xp:
Jordan told Rolling Stone the plan was to play local shows with "other bands that didn't have a place in the city's punk or hardcore shows." The Ringer reports that he grew up in Calvert County, Maryland, in the suburbs of Washington, D.C., and moved to Philadelphia in the early 2010s.

Loud Fast Philly, the local DIY interview series, has a conversation with Jordan and Polo about coming up as outsiders in both Black communities and mostly white punk spaces.

yt: Full set, First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, Nov 5, 2016
years.h: Another record with no title, this one on SRA Records
years.p: Untitled LP has jazzier guitar chords than the hardcore around it, and a William Blake poem in the mix.
years.xp: Rolling Stone points to the Blake reference, "The Little Black Boy", as a sign the band was already wider than its hardcore label.

years.h: Old Gray take Soul Glo to Brooklyn and Boston
years.p: A short Northeast weekend run behind Old Gray, among the band's first shows outside Philadelphia.

years.h: GG Guerra arrives on bass and samples
years.p: Gianmarco "GG" Guerra is a multi-instrumentalist, producer and programmer, and the band's sound leans on him from here.

years.cap: On drums at The Atlantic, Gainesville, Feb 4, 2019
years.h: TJ Stevenson takes over Jamie Sokol's drum stool
years.p: [[Pierce Jordan|6a8a8824-41e0-422e-a17e-b9b0517d89f2]], Polo, Guerra and Stevenson are the lineup that makes the next three records.

years.big: "truly held together by dried tears and blood"
years.h: Missouri troopers stop the van and arrest GG Guerra
years.p: The Missouri State Highway Patrol arrests Guerra on the way to a show in St. Louis. The band raises $15,000 for his bail.
years.xp: A 2021 band statement quoted by The Ringer lists "constant van issues, mental issues, shit w the law" as the cost of touring, and sums up the band as "truly held together by dried tears and blood."

eras.title: Everything goes in the record
eras.text: With the 2019 LP, Soul Glo stops sounding like a screamo revival and starts pulling in hip-hop, noise and jazz fusion. A pandemic-year EP keeps the pace.

years.cap: Jordan at The Atlantic, Gainesville, Feb 4, 2019
years.src: The Ringer · Rolling Stone · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: The Nigga in Me Is Me leaves the screamo revival behind
years.p: The SRA Records LP pulls in hip-hop, noise and jazz fusion, and Jordan's confrontational titles become the band's calling card.
years.xp: Jordan has said the original idea was a hardcore band that could use a word most hardcore audiences avoid, and make a room uncomfortable enough to keep listening. The single from the record, "Too Late, Nigger I'm Tired", shows the method.

years.h: Songs to Yeet at the Sun goes out on Secret Voice
years.p: The EP has the singles "(Quietly) Do the Right Thing" and "29", and it's the last release before the Epitaph deal.

eras.title: From bail fund to Epitaph
eras.text: In 2018 the band raised $15,000 to get its bassist out of a Missouri jail. In 2021 it's on Epitaph and puts out two EPs.

years.h: Soul Glo sign to Epitaph and release two DisNigga EPs
years.p: DisNigga, Vol. 1 and DisNigga, Vol. 2 are their first releases for Epitaph.

eras.title: Diaspora Problems
eras.text: The record that puts Soul Glo on year-end lists arrives in the same months the band loses its guitarist and rebuilds around two new bassists.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: Ruben Polo is out, and Rob Blackwell and Leon Da Boss are in on bass
years.p: Polo, a founding guitarist, departs after an ex-boyfriend accused him of rape by deception, according to Rolling Stone; Polo denies it.
years.xp:
The Ringer noted Polo's exit, along with a cancelled Circa Survive opening slot, in the weeks before release. It says Polo left after the album was recorded and Jordan declined to say why. TJ Stevenson called the cancelled slot "a victim of poor circumstances. And COVID. A wicked confluence of bullshit."

Guerra moved from bass to guitar and programming, and Rob Blackwell and Leon Da Boss came in on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Diaspora Problems · Album of the Year · Bandcamp Daily · The Ringer · Brooklyn Vegan
years.h: Pitchfork gives Diaspora Problems an 8.5 and ranks it No. 36 of 2022
years.p: Metacritic scores the Epitaph debut 86, and Wikipedia dates the release March 25, 2022.
years.xp:
The Ringer says it was recorded from December 2020 to August 2021, produced by Guerra and Evan Bernard with Will Yip on mix and master. The title comes from a Facebook event, where a promoter's blurb for Soul Glo read only "Philadelphia, diaspora problems", Jordan told Bandcamp Daily. On the sound, he told the same interview: "nobody really was gonna want to listen to me scream for 40 minutes straight."

Guests are people Jordan already knew, with the exception of Mother Maryrose: McKinley Dixon and Lojii, Kathryn Edwards of Thirdface, Philly rapper Zula Wildheart and BEARCAT. Elsewhere Vulture had it at No. 5, The Wire at No. 12 and NPR at No. 49; Rolling Stone later put it in its 100 Greatest Punk Albums, and Riot Fest's page calls it Best New Music.

years.h: The lead single "Jump!! (Or Get Jumped!!!((by the future)))" gets a video
years.p: Out in January 2022, the Epitaph video is the first look at the new record's mix of breakneck hardcore and hip-hop.

years.h: Show Me the Body and Wifigawd join Soul Glo on the Half-a-USA tour
years.p: A cross-country run, with Show Me the Body and Wifigawd on the bill.

years.h: Soul Glo and Turnstile open for My Chemical Romance in an arena
years.p: The reunion show is at PNC Arena in North Carolina, with [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]] on the same bill.

yt: Live at Mohawk Place, Buffalo, Nov 14, 2022
years.h: City of Caterpillar and Thirdface share a Northeast bill with Soul Glo
years.p: Soul Glo co-headline with the screamo band City of Caterpillar and Philadelphia's Thirdface, closing the loop on the band's earliest influences.

eras.title: Coachella, then a new record
eras.text: Soul Glo plays a big festival stage, adds a third bassist and announces a follow-up with Mannequin Pussy on it.

yt: Live on KEXP at THING Festival, Aug 25, 2023
years.h: Jordan plays Coachella in a thong, as he'd joked he would
years.p: At the 22nd Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, Rolling Stone says he ran around in a thong "that made him look perfectly nude."
years.xp: Rolling Stone says Jordan had joked about performing naked at the festival. It dates the Coachella set 2024; Wikipedia gives 2023.

yt: Full set, The Secret History of Black Punk Fest II, Nov 9, 2024
years.p: Wikipedia lists Hightower as the third person in the bass slot since 2022, alongside Blackwell and Da Boss.

years.cap: Soul Glo at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C., June 5, 2026
years.h: Soul Glo announce Na I'm Gon Grab Allat for January 15, 2027
years.p: The lead single "February Theory" features [[Mannequin Pussy|e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4]]. Jordan calls the album "largely about failures, mine and others, in my relationships with different men in my life."
years.xp:
Kerrang lists guests including Bear Regisford of Mannequin Pussy, Tati Salazar of Commitment, Tunde Adebimpe, MIKE, BbyNutha and Eugene Robinson.

Riot Fest's page lists a Friday 1:30 p.m. set for the band on its Rise Stage.
